EMERGENCY CRITERIA
A LEVEL (1) EMERGENCY  AT THE SILVERBERRY SITE IS A STATE THAT WOULD
FORCE NORMAL OPERATIONS TO BE TEMPORARILY SUSPENDED
OR SHUT DOWN.
A LEVEL (1) EMERGENCY WOULD PRESENT NO DANGER TO C.C.S.
PERSONNEL OR TO THE PUBLIC AROUND OR NEAR THE SILVERBERRY
SITE.
C.C.S. PERSONNEL AND EQUIP

CCS will designate an environmental inspector to ensure that this C&R plan and any
other applicable environmental requirements are adhered to.

1) To mitigate the potential impacts, topsoil will be salvaged from all areas that will
be disturbed by landfill construction.
1) All construction activities will be restricted to the designated surveyed project site.
All construction traffic will adhere to safety and traffic regulations.

2) To prevent introduction of weedy species to the area, all equipment will be
washed with high pressure water or steam to remove any remnant mud and
vegetative debris prior to entering the project site.  Equipment will not be allowed
on the project site if has not been properly cleaned.

4) Adequate fire fighting equipment will be available on site.  In the event of a fire,
the Contractor will immediately use resources required to contain the fire.  The
Emergency Response Plan will be activated if any fire cannot be immediately
controlled.

5) If a previously unidentified archaeological and/or heritage site is encountered
during construction, no further construction will be undertaken in the immediate
vicinity until the site has been examined by a qualified archaeologist.
Construction activity will not re-commence without consultation

7) If conditions become such that significant erosion is occurring during construction,
erosion control measures such as silt fences, straw bales, or other suitable means
will be used to control the erosion.

4) Used oil, filter and grease cartridges, lubrication containers, and other products of
equipment maintenance and/or repair will be collected and disposed of at an

1) CCS Silverberry will keep all appropriate regulatory personnel and adjacent
landowners informed of project developments throughout all phases of
construction.

1) Project related wildlife deaths and nuisance animals will be reported immediately
to the appropriate British Columbia Ministry of Water, Land and Air Protection,
Wildlife Branch representative.

2) The feeding or harassment of livestock or wildlife will be prohibited.  Construction
personnel will not be permitted to have firearms or pets on the project site.  All
food and wastes will be stored and secured in vehicles or appropriate facilities.
